newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Congress doubts time for labor reform.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Congress doubts time for labor reform.

text.p: The head of the ruling party bloc in Argentina's lower house of Congress said it was increasingly unlikely that legislators would pass proposed labor reforms that the government demands this year.
President Carlos Menem has threatened to impose by decree the plan that would scrap collective bargaining and make workers' hours and conditions more flexible.
In an interview with Clarin newspaper published Tuesday, Jorge Matzkin, whip of the Peronist party in the Chamber of Deputies, said there is still no consensus.
"The proposals were introduced almost two months ago and there is hardly one point of agreement between the parties: the government, the CGT (labor confederation) and businessmen," Matzkin said.

"This implies a lack of ability to reach consensus and the responsibility is not ours. Furthermore, it's a very long debate, which will require many days, and we have little time and many issues before the end of the year."
The government insists labor reform is critical to help ease the burden of worker benefits on employers and reduce an unemployment rate of 17 percent.
-- Gary Regenstreif, Buenos Aires newsroom, 541 318-0618 RE
